#5007. XRP, Cardano, Polygon Face Brutal Snub as Crypto Executive Exposes Why He’s Avoiding These Altcoins in 2026

Are Ripple’s XRP, Cardano (ADA), and Polygon (POL) losing their appeal among crypto investors in 2026? Ben Simpson, founder of crypto investment platform Collective Shift, has named all three among six altcoins he says he wouldn’t touch with a 10-foot pole, citing concerns ranging from weak network activity and questionable valuations to intensifying competition. His blunt assessment raises fresh questions about which altcoins have the strongest fundamentals to survive the increasingly competitive crypto market.

In his post on X, Simpson acknowledged XRP’s role in enabling near-instant, inexpensive payments on the XRP Ledger but argued that the token lacks a compelling mechanism for capturing the value generated by Ripple’s business growth.

XRP enables fast, low-cost payments on the XRP Ledger.My issue with XRP is it's "value capture".When a business grows, I want to see how that success benefits the token I'm holding. In this case, there is none. Ripple can grow its revenue, but holders don't receive those…

His main concern is that Ripple’s commercial success does not necessarily translate into direct financial benefits for XRP holders. Even as the San Francisco-headquartered company expands its revenue and boosts its payment operations, investors do not receive a share of those profits.

He also pointed out that Ripple does not use its business earnings to buy back XRP, a mechanism that could potentially create additional demand for the token. For Simpson, the absence of both profit-sharing and a buyback program makes it difficult to establish a direct link between Ripple’s growing business and XRP’s price in the long term.

He considers these shortcomings significant enough to keep XRP off his investment list, despite the network’s payment capabilities.

Simpson also expressed reservations about Cardano, arguing that its adoption level does not justify its market valuation. Although ADA powers a blockchain designed to support smart contracts and decentralized applications, he believes the network is generating relatively little economic activity compared with its overall market size.

To support his argument, Simpson pointed to Cardano’s fee generation, claiming that the network collected just $140,000 in transaction fees over a 30-day period despite ADA carrying a market capitalization of approximately $7.5 billion.

For him, the disparity raises questions about whether Cardano is attracting enough users and developers to sustain its valuation. He believes a blockchain with such a substantial market capitalization should demonstrate considerably stronger usage and demand for its services.

Ultimately, Simpson’s concern is that Cardano needs to translate its technological ambitions and established ecosystem into greater real-world activity. Without a meaningful increase in network usage, he appears unconvinced that ADA offers an attractive investment proposition.

Polygon also made the list, with concerns centered on the growing competition in Ethereum’s scaling ecosystem. Although POL supports a network designed to make transactions faster and cheaper, the increasing number of competing blockchain solutions has made it harder for Polygon to maintain a distinctive advantage.

Simpson’s concern is that newer networks are offering similar benefits, including lower transaction costs and faster processing speeds, leaving Polygon with fewer obvious ways to differentiate itself.

With several projects competing for developers, users, and blockchain activity, POL faces the challenge of proving why it deserves a place ahead of its rivals.

Beyond XRP, Cardano, and Polygon, three other cryptocurrencies also fell short of Ben Simpson’s investment criteria: Sui (SUI), Ronin (RON), and Dogwifhat (WIF). Unlike his concerns about the first three crypto projects, his reservations about these tokens stem largely from changing investment convictions, disappointing adoption, and excessive reliance on market hype.

Sui was among the projects Simpson previously held before changing his investment outlook. The high-speed blockchain is designed to support decentralized applications and transactions, but he eventually dumped his SUI holdings at a loss of between 20% and 30% after his investment thesis changed. He did not elaborate on the specific developments that prompted his decision.

Ronin was another project he abandoned after its growth failed to match his expectations. Initially attracted by the potential of blockchain gaming, the pundit bought into the network, which uses RON for transaction fees and staking. However, the anticipated expansion in gaming adoption did not materialize as he had hoped, prompting him to exit the position relatively quickly. He argued that strong sector potential means little without meaningful retail participation.

WIF, meanwhile, represented a different kind of investment mistake. Simpson admitted that his decision to buy the Solana-based meme coin was driven largely by hype rather than underlying fundamentals. After his investment thesis changed, he sold his holdings to limit further losses.

His experience with WIF appears to have reinforced his preference for cryptocurrencies backed by stronger fundamentals rather than speculative excitement.

RLUSD briefly overtakes Trump’s USD1 stablecoin at $2.87B, while XRP struggles below $1 amid persistent selling pressure.

Following the latest Ripple news, RLUSD (Ripple’s stablecoin) reached a new milestone over the weekend, with its circulating supply hitting a record $2.87 billion on Saturday, November 21. The surge also pushed RLUSD ahead of USD1, the stablecoin issued by the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial.

Ripple's $RLUSD hits a new all-time high of $2.874 billion in circulating supply, surpassing Trump's USD1 stablecoin.@Ripple pic.twitter.com/TlokhQ8Se8

— MSB Intel (@MSBIntel) November 23, 2026

The lead did not last, though. On Tuesday, RLUSD’s supply slipped to $2.82 billion, while USD1 held at about $2.85 billion.

The two coins are now separated by about $30 million, and they are heading in opposite directions. RLUSD has more than doubled in a year. USD1 has lost almost half its supply since February.

Meanwhile, XRP, the token closely tied to Ripple, trades near $0.93, down 26% this month.

So how did Ripple’s dollar catch up, and does it help XRP?

We pulled the daily supply of both coins from DefiLlama’s stablecoin dashboard, which adds up every chain they run on.

We also checked the contracts directly. RLUSD has $2.04 billion on Ethereum and $761 million on the XRP Ledger. USD1 is spread across BNB Chain ($1.10 billion), Solana ($868 million) and Ethereum ($852 million).

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

RLUSD’s growth has come in steps. Supply jumped from about $1.5 billion to $2.4 billion in August, then climbed again from late October.

Ripple has pushed it hard, and that push is behind most Ripple news this autumn. In October, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency gave Ripple National Trust Bank final approval to manage RLUSD’s reserves. Robinhood expanded its RLUSD deal the same month. Binance has also run repeated campaigns that pay XRP to RLUSD holders.

USD1 is moving the other way. Its supply rose quickly early in 2026, then fell from $4.47 billion on October 7 to $2.85 billion now.

The XRP Ledger matters most for XRP holders. About $761 million of RLUSD sits there, roughly a quarter of the total. That is where RLUSD activity can create demand for XRP, which pays the ledger’s fees.

EXPLORE: Trump Media Moves $344 Million in Bitcoin to Crypto.com as TRUMP Hits a Record Low: How Are Trump’s Crypto Ventures Doing?

The problem is, for XRP holders, the RLUSD Ripple news has not translated into buying yet. We measured taker flows on Binance’s XRP/USDT spot market, meaning trades where the buyer or seller crossed the spread. Sellers outweighed buyers on six of the last seven days, for a net $25.5 million. Over 30 days, the net selling reached $140 million.

The selling is fading, though. It dropped from $17 million on November 14 to $2.1 million on Monday. A cross-exchange flow chart shared by traders showed spot buyers absorbing futures selling on Monday, with $11.7 million of net spot buying against $26.9 million of futures selling.

XRP trades at $0.9295, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1.1499, and its 200-day EMA at $1.2996.

The next Ripple news test is whether RLUSD can retake the lead and hold it. For XRP, the signal to watch is simpler: a daily close back above $1.00 while sellers keep fading.

#5005. Why Bitcoin Fell Below $60K Despite Nvidia’s 31% Surge

Home » Crypto Market News » Why Bitcoin Fell Below $60K Despite Nvidia’s 31% Surge

While tech stocks celebrated Jensen Huang’s return, on-chain metrics suggest crypto traders face a very different test.

Bitcoin (BTC) briefly fell to $59,400 after failing to sustain a rally triggered by Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO —largely because the bounce was fueled by short-lived enthusiasm rather than genuine spot demand or improved crypto fundamentals.

While Nvidia (NVDA) shares surged more than 30% and major U.S. stock indexes recorded one of their best sessions in years on Monday, November 23, Bitcoin’s price reversed its initial recovery within about 12 hours, raising questions about buying demand across the cryptocurrency market.

Bitcoin climbed toward an intraday high of $64,500 following Nvidia’s announcement before retreating below $60,000. The reversal contrasted with Nvidia’s 31% gain, the Nasdaq’s 6.51% advance and the S&P 500’s 4.73% increase.

According to Santiment’s latest market intelligence report, Bitcoin’s initial recovery was driven mainly by a wave of optimism and FOMO across financial markets, rather than any real improvement in demand for BTC.

Santiment’s Trending Words Dashboard recorded a sharp increase in mentions of Nvidia and Jensen Huang across cryptocurrency discussions on November 23, producing the largest single-day spike over the past month.

“Huang’s return provided an immediate reason for investors to become more confident in Nvidia and its surrounding AI ecosystem,” the Santiment report states. “However, nothing about the announcement directly improved Bitcoin’s adoption, increased demand for BTC, or resolved the selling pressure that had dominated cryptocurrency markets for weeks.”

Still, the report noted that AI and big data altcoins could hold long-term potential. For Bitcoin, however, rather than confirming a new bullish trend, the rally became another example of how FOMO can punish traders who mistake a temporary market reaction for a lasting shift in fundamentals.

Despite the underwhelming price action, Santiment’s on-chain data highlighted an unexpected divergence.

Around November 20, the analytics firm recorded roughly 750,400 daily active addresses and 332,820 new addresses, pointing to a notable rise in network participation even as prices weakened.

Daily active addresses measure how many unique blockchain addresses participate in transactions, while network growth tracks newly created active addresses.

Both metrics climbed during the downturn, indicating that underlying blockchain usage remained resilient despite falling market value.

Santiment cautioned that the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday may introduce another layer of uncertainty. Trading activity typically thins out during holiday-shortened weeks, allowing smaller groups of buyers and sellers to trigger outsized price swings amid lower liquidity.

Markets are also looking ahead to Wednesday’s October PCE inflation report and the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book, both of which could shift rate expectations ahead of the Fed’s December 8–9 policy meeting.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin traders are watching for a potential retest of the $56,000 level, which could mark a local market bottom.

#5004. Shiba Inu (SHIB) Community Builds New Shibarium Explorer While Shytoshi Kusama Stays Silent

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) community members have launched a new block explorer for Shibarium, the layer-2 network of the SHIB ecosystem, and Shiba Inu lead Shytoshi Kusama has remained silent on X since May.

Shiba Inu community veteran Mazrael announced the new explorer, scan.shibfun.app, in an X post. "Shibarium has a new block explorer," he wrote. According to Mazrael, the explorer was "built by the community, powered by ShibWatch, dressed in the Eternity Hub look."

The launch comes as SHIB trades near its lowest levels in years. In November, the price of SHIB fell as low as $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021, and on Nov. 22, the token traded at around $0.00000362, according to CoinMarketCap.

According to the post, users can type a .shib name in the search bar and land on the wallet linked to it, and the explorer also shows new Shiboshis from Shibarium every day. For developers, Mazrael listed contract verification, read and write functions for contracts, the activity of ERC-4337 smart wallets, and a free API, which he described as "Etherscan-style too." Method names are decoded as well, and in Mazrael's words, there are "no more mystery 0x codes." The explorer also has a DApps page with Shibarium games and apps, and a button that adds Shibarium to a wallet in one click.

The work on the explorer is not finished yet. "Live blocks are complete now, and older history indexing," Mazrael wrote. On Tuesday, the explorer itself showed that 3% of Shibarium blocks had been indexed, and a notice on the site said that some of the counts may be inaccurate. Mazrael added that the new explorer can be found on Shib.io under ShibWatch.

Shytoshi Kusama's last post or interaction on X dates back to May 13, 2026. In September, Kusama changed his X bio to "Polish" and his location to "Close," and he has not explained the meaning of either word. The official Shibarium account on X has not posted since July 13, 2026.

Still, Shibarium updates kept coming from community members. In October, Mazrael said that CreateX, a standard factory for deploying contracts at the same address on different chains, went live on Shibarium. According to Mazrael, all 12 Safe v1.4.1 contracts were deployed to their canonical addresses through the Safe Singleton Factory, and x402 went live too, so AI agents can now pay in SHIB, TREAT and wrapped BONE.

In September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge and withdrew about $2.4 million worth of assets from it.

According to Shibariumscan, Shibarium processed 546 transactions in a single day in late November, and on Oct. 31, the daily number of transactions on the network was 6,370. Since its launch in August 2023, Shibarium has processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in total.

At the same time, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan.

#5003. RLUSD supply grew 30% on Ethereum and fell 20% on XRPL – Assessing…

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

RLUSD is growing while USDT and USDC are losing supply.

At the macro level, the stablecoin sector is in a relatively weak phase. In Q4 alone, the market lost over $20 billion of value. As a result, the overall stablecoin market cap has fallen below $300 billion.

This means that all of the market’s growth since Q3 2025 (when it peaked at above $320 billion) has been erased. Notably, USDT and USDC account for more than half of the total liquidity outflows during this period.

In contrast, RLUSD has increased by almost 20% during this period. This represents an increase of almost $500 million in total supply, pushing its total market cap to a record $2.9 billion.

In essence, RLUSD is attracting fresh liquidity even as the broader stablecoin market continues to contract.

This raises an important question: Which L1 stands to benefit the most from this growth?

Fundamentally, Ethereum supports much larger amounts of RLUSD in comparison to XRPL, with 72%+ of RLUSD ($2.08 billion) on Ethereum. In addition, supply growth on Ethereum is relatively higher.

In the last 30 days, RLUSD supply has increased by 30% on Ethereum, whereas supply has fallen by 20% on XRPL.

So, with RLUSD liquidity increasingly concentrated on Ethereum even as the broader stablecoin market faces outflows, Ethereum seems to be the clear winner. However, supply is only one side of the story, and XRPL’s transaction volume shows why it should not be overlooked.

Growing stablecoin supply and actually using that supply are two different things.

Interestingly, this difference is becoming important in comparing Ethereum [ETH] and XRPL’s on-chain activity around RLUSD. On-chain data shows that nearly $11.716 billion worth of RLUSD was transacted on the XRP Ledger and Ethereum in the week up to the 1st of November 2026.

The key takeaway? XRPL handled the larger share of RLUSD activity. As the chart below shows, $6.699 billion was transacted on the XRPL network, representing 57% of the total RLUSD volume. The Ethereum blockchain had total transactions of $5.017 billion (42.82%).

So, although there is more RLUSD on the Ethereum blockchain, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume.

Notably, RLUSD’s DEX activity on XRPL is also picking up.

The total DEX volume reached an all-time high of $596.2 million in the week ending August. While volume has dropped in recent weeks, it has been consistently above $70 million per week for the last 10 weeks.

More recently, volume has picked up again, exceeding $200 million per week. This is significantly higher than previous averages of approximately $15 million.

So, while there is more RLUSD on Ethereum, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume and growing DEX activity. This suggests that more RLUSD is being used on XRPL, making it a network to watch as the stablecoin continues to grow.

RLUSD supply is growing despite broader stablecoin outflows, with Ethereum holding over 72% of its total supply.

XRPL handles 57% of RLUSD transaction volume and is seeing a sharp rise in DEX activity.

#5002. Flop Labs Pushes Back Testnet Launch Amid Final Preparations

Flop Labs has announced a minor delay to the launch of its public testnet, pushing back from its previous goal of 15:00 (UTC+8) on November 24.

It's unclear what the reason for the delay is, although the team does expect to launch the testnet before 18:00 (UTC+8) the same day.

Possible reasons for the delay could include conducting final checks, calibrating nodes, validator onboarding, load testing, etc. (although Flop Labs has not confirmed any of these to be the reason for the delay).

It does not appear that Flop Labs has any plans to move the testnet launch to another day.

Flop Labs is building FLOP Network, a blockchain serving as a settlement layer for what it calls the "agentic economy". This would enable AI agents to make payments for computation (e.g. model inference) and memory services, and provide rewards to GPU miners that contribute their computational power to fulfill these requests.

Computation is verified via Flop Labs' "Proof of Useful Inference", which entails miners providing evidence that they've carried out the desired AI computation, and validators checking this evidence.

Why does this matter? FLOP Network would enable agents to make payments for computation, memory, etc. Flop Labs' main competitors include Akash Network and io.net (both of which facilitate access to compute/gpu resources in a decentralized manner), as well as Render Network (which started out facilitating decentralized graphics rendering but has since expanded into AI/compute more broadly).

While Flop Labs' competitors also facilitate access to compute, Flop Labs' main differentiating factor appears to be its focus on facilitating agent-to-agent commerce and computation-verification.

Flop Labs is led by Arthur Hayes, co-founder of crypto exchange BitMEX and current chief investment officer at Maelstrom. The rest of Flop Labs' team includes Sergey Vidyuk (ex-Deutsche Bank/BitMEX) as CTO, and Shu Duan (with experience in investment banking and crypto asset management) as chief strategy officer.

The testnet would be an opportunity to see if Flop Labs can successfully build out its envisioned agentic economy.

#5001. JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX Trade Digital Gold in London as Tokenized Gold Holdings Jump 48%

London is testing tokenized gold as Tether Gold and PAX Gold holdings climb 48% to $4.6 billion despite falling gold prices.

JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX completed the first live wholesale trades of fractional tokenized gold in London last week. The test is meant to keep the world’s largest gold market ahead of Asian rivals. The three firms also used the digital gold as collateral, without moving a single bar out of the vaults.

Bloomberg reported the trades on Tuesday. They ran on a system built by the World Gold Council (WGC), the industry body that led the project. David Tait, the WGC’s chief executive, called it “a historic step forward for the gold market.”

JPMORGAN $JPM, HSBC AND STONEX COMPLETE THE FIRST LIVE WHOLESALE TRADES OF FRACTIONAL DIGITAL GOLD IN LONDON, ALSO USING IT AS COLLATERAL pic.twitter.com/bwVAdrpkXh

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) November 24, 2026

The banks did not say how much gold changed hands. The system is still in testing, and there is no date yet for a wider launch. The timing is awkward for gold itself. The metal trades near $3,626 an ounce, 32% below its January record and 11% lower than a year ago.

What changes for London’s bullion market, and does it matter for crypto’s own gold tokens?

The WGC calls the new format “pooled gold interests.” Each one is a fractional, electronically transferable share in a pool of physical bars held in approved London vaults.

That fills a gap. Most London trades today are in unallocated gold, which is cheap to hold but leaves buyers as creditors if their bank fails. Allocated gold means owning specific bars, which is safer but costly and hard to split. The WGC proposed the pooled model with law firm Linklaters in September 2025 as a third route between the two.

The collateral piece matters most. Banks could pledge gold for loans and margin as easily as they post bonds, without trucks or vault transfers.

London has a lot riding on it. Its over-the-counter market handles more than $180 billion of gold trades a day, and its vaults held $1.4 trillion of gold in August. Hong Kong, working with the Shanghai Gold Exchange, began testing its own gold clearing system in July.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The London pilot is a closed, bank-only system. Crypto has run its own version for years with Tether Gold (XAUT) and PAX Gold (PAXG), and those tokens have been growing fast.

We read the supply of both tokens straight from their Ethereum contracts, where each token equals one troy ounce. We compared that with CoinGecko’s figures from a year ago.

So crypto’s digital gold kept adding ounces even as the gold price fell. Still, the two tokens hold about 0.33% of the value of gold sitting in London’s vaults. The whole tokenized gold category traded about $329 million in the past 24 hours on CoinGecko, against London’s $180 billion a day.

Explore: RLUSD Surpasses Trump’s USD1 Stablecoin but XRP Still Sinks 26%

PAX Gold tracks the metal closely. On Binance, PAXG trades at $3,637, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $3,945, and its 200-day EMA at $4,195.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it to $3,491 on Saturday, its lowest level in 300 days. Sellers led on Binance’s spot market, where the token itself changes hands. Orders that sold at the market price right away outweighed buyers by a net $13.4 million over the past seven days.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Coinbase Listings

The WGC still has to settle governance rules and a launch date. If the big banks adopt digital gold for collateral, the gap between London’s vaults and crypto’s gold tokens could start to close.

Purchase your first BTC in under 10 minutes while avoiding bank blocks and fees.

Buying Bitcoin with a credit card is the fastest way to go from zero to owning crypto—often taking less than ten minutes from account creation to holding BTC in your wallet. While bank transfers can drag on for days, swiping your Visa or Mastercard gives you instant market exposure.

However, convenience comes with a catch. Not all crypto exchanges accept credit cards, some banks block crypto transactions outright, and high “cash advance” fees can silently eat into your investment if you don’t know what to look for.

Whether you are making your very first crypto purchase or simply want the quickest checkout method available, this step-by-step guide walks you through the exact process, breaks down the real costs, and shows you how to avoid rookie mistakes.

To keep the process smooth and avoid getting stuck mid-transaction, gather these four essentials before opening an account:

Follow these five straightforward steps to complete your purchase safely.

You cannot buy Bitcoin directly through your bank’s app. You need a regulated crypto exchange that acts as a bridge between your credit card and the Bitcoin network. Look for platforms with strong security track records, transparent fee structures, and instant card processing.

Top beginner-friendly platforms that support credit cards include:

Once you pick a platform, sign up using your email address and create a strong, unique password. Immediately enable Two-Factor Authentication using an authenticator app (like Google Authenticator) rather than SMS text messages, which are vulnerable to SIM-swap attacks.

Next, complete the identity verification process:

Most major exchanges automate this process, approving your account within 2 to 5 minutes.

Navigate to your account’s Payment Methods or Billing settings and select Add a Credit/Debit Card. Enter your 16-digit card number, expiration date, CVV security code, and billing address.

Pro tip: Make sure the billing address on your exchange account matches your credit card statement word-for-word. Even a minor mismatch will trigger an automatic fraud decline.

Head to the Buy Crypto section, select Bitcoin (BTC) as the asset you want to receive, and choose your linked credit card as the payment method.

Enter the amount you want to spend in your local currency (e.g., $100 or €100). Before hitting confirm, pause on the order preview screen and check two numbers:

Once you confirm the order, the exchange charges your card and credits your Bitcoin balance immediately.

Congratulations—you officially own Bitcoin! Right now, your BTC is sitting in your exchange’s custodial wallet. If you only bought a small amount (50–200) to get started, leaving it on a major, regulated exchange is fine while you learn the ropes.

However, if you plan to hold significant value long-term, transfer your Bitcoin to a self-custody wallet (such as a Ledger or Trezor hardware wallet, or a reputable mobile wallet like BlueWallet).

In crypto, holding your own private keys ensures that nobody—not even the exchange—can freeze or lose your funds.

While credit cards offer unmatched speed, they are the most expensive way to buy Bitcoin. Keep these three financial realities in mind so you aren’t surprised by your next bank statement:

The Golden Rule: Never buy Bitcoin on credit if you cannot pay off the card balance in full before your next billing cycle. Paying 25% interest on a volatile asset is a quick way to lose money even if Bitcoin’s price goes up.

#4998. Trezor Tells Crypto Users Never to Enter Wallet Backups on Phones Amid Theft Probe

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Crypto wallet provider Trezor has issued a security warning to cryptocurrency users following a recent theft report: "Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website."

According to Onchain Lens, a user reported losing over $600,000 across TRON and Solana while using an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1. Both the Trezor Safe 7 and the Exodus wallet were reportedly affected. The victim had been using a Trezor Safe 7 for nearly two months.

According to the victim, the Trezor wallet arrived sealed, with no visible tampering; the recovery phrase was generated on the Trezor screen and not on the iPhone; the seed was written on paper and never stored digitally. The victim used Trezor Suite on an iPhone 17 Pro Max via Bluetooth and also had the Exodus wallet on the same iPhone.

The device was running iOS 27.2.1, and the victim never approved the unauthorized transactions. The Trezor wallets for TRON and Solana shared one recovery phrase.

The user said $580,000 was stolen from Trezor on TRON and that an unauthorized transaction moved 49,999 USDT on Nov. 21, 2026. The transaction used the default owner permission, making the signing authority central to the investigation.

Another $23,400 was drained from Trezor on Solana, and the victim says they never approved that transfer using the hardware device. The iPhone remains the main focus, as both Trezor Suite and Exodus were reportedly used on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1, and both were affected.

Trezor is designed to keep private keys inside the hardware device. However, compromising the phone alone should not normally provide access to Trezor's private keys, and the mechanism behind both thefts remains largely unknown.

On November 9, 2026, Apple issued iOS 27.2.1, which patched several security holes (including some related to Bluetooth). The victim was reportedly running this version when the theft occurred. Thus, there is currently no evidence connecting those vulnerabilities to these transactions. Possible causes outlined included compromised recovery credentials, unauthorized signing, or a device or software security failure.

Trezor responded to this disclosure, saying that Trezor wallets don’t get drained out of nowhere and that there are currently no reports of funds being stolen remotely from any device. It noted that similar cases usually trace back to a compromised wallet backup.

@OnchainLens @binance @Bybit_Official UPDATE: This device came directly from Trezor and shows no sign of an implant. We’re still investigating what happened. So far there’s no confirmed loss of funds from implants and no implant found in any Trezor Safe 7. Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.

In a further update, Trezor confirmed that the device affected came directly from the company and showed no sign of an implant. The wallet provider added that it continues to investigate what happened.

This appears to be a standalone case, as Trezor reiterated that, so far, no confirmed loss of funds from implants has been reported, and no implant has been found in any Trezor Safe 7. It also reiterated an important security warning: users should never enter their wallet backups into a phone, application, or website.

#4997. Ethereum vs. Nvidia: $3T stock market comeback exposes ETH’s weak demand

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The past 24 hours have delivered a reality check to investors.

Following weeks of selling due to the Jensen Huang situation, around $8 trillion was wiped off the U.S. stock market. However, on the 23rd of November, following the re-appointment of the CEO, almost $3 trillion flowed back almost immediately. NVDA soared by more than 31% and gained back two weeks’ worth of value in one day, showing how quickly sentiment can shift when uncertainty fades.

However, the same recovery did not spill over into crypto. Ethereum initially rose above $1,800 only for it to then trend back down to around the $1,700 mark by the close. The key takeaway? Capital is returning to stocks, but crypto is struggling to attract the same demand. This growing divergence has put “ETH vs. NVDA” at the center of a new debate over where investors see better opportunities.

Interestingly, investors are using five-year returns to make their case.

One post pointed out that investing $10,000 in ETH 5 years ago would now be worth approximately $4,200, marking a 58% loss. This pales in comparison to the over $12,500 that the same investment in NVDA would now be worth, delivering a 25% gain. That’s an $8,300 gap in return on the same investment, adding to the debate over whether investors now see better opportunities in stocks than in crypto.

In this context, the past 24 hours have delivered a reality check for investors. This raises a key question: Is the ongoing ETH distribution  indicative of this change in long-term ownership as money flows once again into stocks? And could this put further pressure on Ethereum [ETH] and ETH-heavy treasury firms?

The past 24 hours have brought some much-needed relief for digital asset treasuries.

It appears that the current NVDA outperformance is boosting sentiment in the U.S. stock market generally, with almost $3 trillion re-entering. In crypto too, several treasury stocks are benefiting. BitMine, for example, has surged by over 11% and recorded its best weekly inflow in more than 3 months. This suggests that improving sentiment could also be supporting demand for ETH-focused companies.

However, Ethereum’s spot flows tell a different story. As shown below, a whale sent a further 85,500 ETH (around $146.98 million) to Binance. Over the past seven days, the same whale has deposited 176,000 ETH (worth approximately $309.21 million) into the exchange. Furthermore, institutional sentiment continues to be negative. BlackRock has seen net withdrawals of 1 million+ ETH, valued at $1.75 billion since October.

This creates a clear divergence: ETH-focused stocks are recovering, while spot market flows continue to signal selling pressure.

That shifts the focus back to the Ethereum vs. Nvidia debate. While treasury stocks are recovering, whales continue to sell, and institutions are also exiting. This suggests that there is still weak demand for spot crypto. Investors seem to be moving away from crypto and into equities.

If this trend continues, it could suggest a broader change in the long-term holding strategy of investors. Whales may not just be selling ETH at random but could be actively moving funds out of the asset and into equities such as NVDA.

NVDA is gaining, but Ethereum is still struggling to attract buyers.

Whale selling could signal a shift from ETH to stocks like NVDA.

#4996. HBAR Price Hits a Double-Bottom ‘Discount Zone’

Home » Altcoins » HBAR Price Hits a Double-Bottom ‘Discount Zone’

Big-timers are hedging the long-term accumulation zone after Hedera dropped below confluent resistance.

Hedera Hashgraph’s native HBAR coin is coiling within a macro ‘discount zone’, analyst Karl Moon notes. In his latest HBAR analysis based on the weekly crypto charts, HBAR has hit the major demand territory between $0.03525 to $0.0516, bouncing off to approximately $0.0555 very briefly.

$HBAR is entering the deep discount zone.Macro range lows are getting very close.This is where bulls need to start showing up. pic.twitter.com/zOfRD6DjuX

Next up, a confluent resistance area at $0.07 comes into play. From here, the OG altcoin may retrieve the $0.075 resistance before claiming the quarterly lows above $0.10. The support from big-time crypto investors looking for the bottom will be key: a positive CMF record is driving that trend switch.

As we can see in the HBAR price chart above, the altcoin is still trading inside the Bollinger Band envelope, slightly below the mid-tier Bollinger Band (BOLL) of $0.05166. Meanwhile, the Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) flipped to 0.07, hinting at crypto currency whales buying on the 4-hour time-frame.

Measured by the Bollinger Bands, the $0.0535 level described by Karl Moon is as the upper boundary of Hedera’s (HBAR) ‘discount zone’ perfectly coincides with the Red-Label Bollinger Band, typically intended to mark a bullish trend switch.

However, the Elliott Wave theory presents a dimmer picture. More Crypto Online’s trading team has established that a rebound above roughly $0.12 has been labeled as a Wave 4. The seasoned traders even expect HBAR to break below the 2024 lows.

hedera-hashgraph:native is approaching the 61.8% retracement at $0.046 and the 2024 low. There is no sign of a low yet, and more downside is likely, possibly including a break below the 2024 low. pic.twitter.com/rU6ZKIUURk

The technical view anticipates more downside, including a possible break below the 2024 low, based on wave patterns and lack of reversal evidence in the HBAR/USDT 4-day timeframe. Meanwhile, Futures participants are betting on an HBAR price bounce back.

The 24-hour liquidation stats also point to short-sellers taking in a higher deficit than HBAR’s bulls, accounting for $145.12K and $87.69K in excessively-leveraged position liquidations, per CoinGlass’ real-time data. While some long positions are unwinding, the scene’s still crowded.

Top trader accounts on major exchanges are mostly bullish, eager for this trend to continue.

Overall HBAR Futures volume grew by 83% since the day before, whilst the Open Interest (OI) slid by 4% to drop below $100 million. Bitcoin’s (BTC) ability to stay above $60K will contribute towards setting the near-term tone.

#4995. Solana Price Prediction 2030: Is $2,000 SOL Still on the Table After a 75% Crash?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solana has lost roughly 75% of its value since reaching an all-time high of $294 in January 2025. Large futures traders are leaning bearish, yet institutional analysts continue to see a future in which SOL trades at four digit prices. So, how realistic is a $2,000 Solana price prediction for 2030?

At around $73, SOL is trading at a fraction of the price some of Wall Street’s most optimistic forecasts suggest it could eventually reach. But a steep discount to an analyst’s target does not necessarily make an asset cheap.

NewsBTC examined liquidation heatmaps, whale positions, historical price action, network economics and institutional valuation models to understand where Solana stands today and what it could realistically be worth by the end of the decade.

The findings paint a more complicated picture than either bulls or bears might expect.

Perhaps the most interesting signal right now comes from the derivatives market.

According to a November 23 snapshot from PumpGlass, only around 20% of the tracked Binance whale position value was allocated to longs. Meanwhile, approximately 79% of the broader trader accounts were positioned long.

Although the two figures measure different aspects of market positioning, the divergence is striking. Large traders appear considerably less optimistic than the wider trading crowd.

The average entry price of tracked whale shorts stood near $77.63, compared with $77.05 for whale longs. With SOL trading around $73 at the time of observation, the short side was better positioned.

The on-chain picture offers another reason for caution.

On November 19, blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that two large holders had unstaked a combined 2.31 million SOL worth approximately $169.4 million before transferring the tokens to Coinbase Prime-associated addresses.

Exchange deposits do not necessarily mean those tokens were sold. Institutional investors use custody platforms for several purposes, including collateral management and portfolio rebalancing. Still, the movement is worth monitoring.

What matters now is whether large holders begin accumulating again or whether the recent decline has further to run.

Solana’s liquidation heatmap reveals an interesting battle developing around its current trading range.

PumpGlass identified several concentrations of potentially vulnerable leveraged positions in its November 23, 19:22 UTC observation.

A recovery toward $79 could put considerable pressure on short sellers. Conversely, a breakdown below $69 could expose another wave of leveraged longs to forced closures.

Data from CoinGlass adds another layer to the picture. At 21:31 UTC on November 23, Solana’s futures open interest stood at $3.86 billion, while rolling 24-hour liquidations reached approximately $30.59 million. Shorts accounted for roughly 72% of those liquidations.

SOL had gained around 3.1% over the same rolling period.

The recovery is consistent with some bearish positions being forced out of the market. However, a liquidated short is not the same as a new investor buying SOL for the next four years.

Until stronger spot demand emerges, traders should be careful about interpreting a short squeeze as the beginning of a sustainable recovery.

Liquidation concentrations are modeled estimates, not guaranteed future orders, and can change considerably as traders adjust their positions.

Solana’s price structure has deteriorated considerably since its September recovery.

After closing July near $72.79, SOL climbed to $103 in August and $117.99 in September. The recovery subsequently unraveled, with October closing near $95.35 before prices returned to the low $70s in November.

Looking at SOL’s historical price action on Binance, using the TradingView SOLUSDT market as the chart reference, five key price regions stand out:

The daily Relative Strength Index was in the low 30s in the observed CoinGlass data, suggesting weak momentum and proximity to oversold territory.

But oversold markets can remain oversold.

A sustained recovery above $80 would be the first encouraging development. Reclaiming $95 and subsequently $100 would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control.

On the downside, failure to hold the $65 range would bring Solana’s 2026 low near $60.42 back into focus.

Our technical assessment remains cautious. There is room for a meaningful relief rally, particularly given the nearby short-liquidation exposure, but the broader market structure has yet to establish a convincing reversal.

While Solana’s price has struggled, its blockchain continues to facilitate substantial financial activity.

According to DefiLlama, Solana’s November 23 network metrics included:

There is something particularly interesting about those last two figures.

Applications running on Solana generated considerably more revenue than the chain itself under DefiLlama’s respective measurement definitions.

This highlights what could become Solana’s biggest valuation challenge.

A blockchain can attract substantial activity and billions of dollars in trading volume without its native token capturing a proportional share of that economic value.

Cheap transactions are excellent for adoption. Whether they are equally good for SOL’s valuation is another question entirely.

That is why Solana’s expansion beyond speculative trading could prove so important.

The blockchain’s growing presence in stablecoins, payments and tokenized real-world assets opens the door to financial activity that could persist even when speculative markets cool.

Its infrastructure is also evolving. The Solana Foundation reported the activation of Alpenglow in October 2026, targeting transaction finality near 150 milliseconds. November’s introduction of Solana 1.0 marked another milestone in the network’s development.

Meanwhile, the announced integration with DTCC’s Tokenization Service, expected in the second half of 2027, could represent a meaningful institutional opportunity.

The real test will be how much financial activity these developments ultimately bring onchain, and how much value SOL captures from it.

Institutional research offers a glimpse into how differently analysts view Solana’s future.

VanEck’s October 2023 research produced one of the widest forecast ranges, with its most optimistic scenario placing SOL above $3,200.

Standard Chartered’s Geoffrey Kendrick was reported in February 2026 to have projected a $2,000 Solana price by 2030, partly based on the network’s potential in stablecoin micropayments.

However, the bank’s reported $250 end-of-2026 target looks increasingly difficult to achieve from current levels. Its original research note was not available for independent review.

Perhaps the most interesting analysis comes from Bitwise’s November 2026 research, which connects Solana’s future valuation to tokenized stock trading.

The asset manager’s base case assumes Solana captures 50% of tokenized-stock trading volume in 2031, generating approximately $6.75 billion in annual network economic value.

Applying a 40-times valuation multiple produces an estimated SOL price of $385, based on a projected total supply of 700 million tokens.

The report acknowledges the key dependency:

Most of the price increase depends on how quickly stocks move onchain.

In its bullish scenario, Solana captures 65% of tokenized-stock trading, generating approximately $12.83 billion in network economic value and supporting a modeled price of $1,100.

These assumptions reveal just how much needs to go right before four-digit SOL prices become fundamentally convincing.

Here is something many price predictions overlook: Solana’s token supply will not necessarily remain where it is today.

Unlike Bitcoin, SOL has no fixed maximum supply. Its inflationary issuance framework rewards validators and staking participants, while future governance decisions can influence the rate of supply growth.

With around 592 million SOL currently circulating, we use an illustrative assumption of 690 million total tokens by 2030 for our valuation scenarios.

The numbers put popular price targets into perspective.

These are total-supply valuations rather than projected circulating market capitalizations.

At $2,000, Solana would need to command a valuation of approximately $1.38 trillion under our assumptions.

Using Bitwise’s base-case valuation multiple of 40 times annual network economic value as an illustrative benchmark, Solana would need to generate approximately $34.5 billion in annual economic value to support that figure.

Even at a more generous 60-times multiple, the requirement would be $23 billion annually.

That is substantially more demanding than simply attracting another wave of cryptocurrency traders.

Based on the network’s economic opportunity, competitive landscape, token supply and institutional research, NewsBTC has developed four conditional valuation scenarios.

These ranges are conditional editorial scenarios, not statistically derived forecasts. Outcomes outside these ranges, including substantially greater losses, are possible.

Solana remains relevant but struggles to turn network adoption into meaningful economic value for SOL. Institutional projects develop more slowly than expected, competitors gain market share, and speculative trading remains an important source of demand.

Solana does not need to fail for this scenario to materialize. It only needs to fall short of the expectations investors have placed on it.

Our central expectation assumes Solana retains its position among the leading smart-contract networks while expanding its role in payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets.

Under this scenario, the network does not need to dominate global finance. It needs to establish a durable position within it and capture more economic value from the applications it supports.

Solana becomes a major platform for tokenized equities, stablecoin settlements and high-frequency financial applications.

Institutional adoption moves beyond announcements, network revenue expands significantly, and the broader cryptocurrency market benefits from favorable liquidity conditions.

At $1,000, SOL would trade at approximately 13.8 times its November 23 reference price.

This is where the most ambitious institutional predictions become conceivable.

Solana would need to capture a significant share of a much larger on-chain financial economy, scale its infrastructure accordingly, and translate that activity into sustained demand for SOL.

An exceptional cryptocurrency bull market could also temporarily push valuations beyond what underlying economics justify.

We would not consider this the most likely outcome based on today’s evidence.

Rather than following every new price target, long-term SOL investors may benefit from monitoring five developments:

Competition from Ethereum, its scaling ecosystem and specialized financial networks remains a considerable risk.

If Solana’s transaction volumes rise while the economic value captured by the network stagnates, we would have reason to lower our valuation assumptions, regardless of how impressive the adoption statistics look.

The current market offers an interesting contradiction.

Solana’s blockchain has established a meaningful financial ecosystem, yet its token is trading roughly 75% below its historical record. Large futures traders are cautious, while institutional research continues to outline substantial long-term opportunities.

Our $180 to $400 base-case range for 2030 reflects the possibility that Solana can grow without fulfilling every ambitious expectation placed on it.

A move toward $1,000 is conceivable under considerably stronger conditions. At $2,000, however, investors would be betting on Solana becoming one of the world’s most valuable digital financial networks.

The opportunity is there. The evidence that would justify such a valuation is not there yet.

For now, the most interesting question surrounding Solana is not how many transactions it can process, but how much those transactions will eventually be worth to SOL holders.

NewsBTC’s analysis places Solana between $180 and $400 by 2030 under our base-case scenario. Strong institutional adoption and improved network economics could support a bullish range of $600 to $1,000, while weaker growth could leave SOL trading between $40 and $110.

Solana could reach $500 by 2030 if its adoption across payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets continues to expand. Based on an assumed total supply of 690 million SOL, a $500 price would imply a total-supply valuation of approximately $345 billion.

A $1,000 Solana price is possible under a strong bullish scenario. However, achieving and sustaining that valuation would require substantial institutional adoption, higher network economic value and favorable cryptocurrency market conditions. At $1,000, Solana’s implied total-supply valuation would reach approximately $690 billion.

Standard Chartered was reported to have projected a $2,000 SOL price by 2030 in February 2026. However, our analysis considers this an extreme bullish scenario. Reaching $2,000 would imply a total-supply valuation of approximately $1.38 trillion, requiring extraordinary growth in Solana’s financial ecosystem and demand for SOL.

While mathematically possible, a $10,000 SOL price would imply a valuation of approximately $6.9 trillion based on our 2030 supply assumption. There is currently insufficient economic evidence to support such a valuation within this timeframe.

Solana offers long-term exposure to decentralized finance, stablecoin payments and institutional asset tokenization. However, its investment potential depends on whether growing network adoption translates into sustainable demand for SOL. Competition, token inflation, market volatility and regulatory developments remain significant risks.

Solana could challenge Ethereum in areas such as decentralized trading, payments and financial applications. However, overtaking Ethereum by market capitalization would require substantial growth in Solana’s economic value, institutional demand and developer ecosystem. Higher transaction volumes alone would not guarantee that outcome.

VanEck’s October 2023 research placed SOL at $334.70 in its base case and $3,211.28 in its most optimistic scenario for 2030. Standard Chartered was reported to have projected $2,000 in February 2026, while Bitwise’s November 2026 research estimated a base-case price of $385 and a bullish price of $1,100 for 2031.

Weak spot demand, large-holder selling, leveraged liquidations, network disruptions and deteriorating global liquidity could all contribute to further declines. From a technical perspective, losing the $60 to $65 support region identified in our November 23, 2026 analysis would significantly weaken the recovery outlook.

Using the November 23, 2026 reference price of $72.52, a $1,000 investment would purchase approximately 13.79 SOL.

These hypothetical calculations exclude staking rewards, trading fees and taxes. Actual returns may differ substantially, and investors could lose their entire investment.

This analysis uses CoinGlass and PumpGlass market observations dated November 23, 2026, at 21:31 UTC and 19:22 UTC, respectively. Network metrics are provisional DefiLlama observations dated November 23. Technical analysis uses historical Binance SOLUSDT candles. NewsBTC’s valuation scenarios assume 690 million total SOL in 2030 and are conditional editorial estimates rather than statistical forecasts. #4994. Solana Validators Can Now Stop Block Processing

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

In periods of competing blocks, Solana validators spend CPU and timing resources replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another competing block from the same slot has been finalized.

This PR proposes changes to validator software to help prevent work from being done. It also decouples functionality and gives control to Votor in requesting slot cancellation without modifying BankForks.

Overall, this is a reasonable technical improvement and has a good engineering motivation. Further technical comments and review would be helpful to understand if there are potential race conditions or issues with reliability of replay and consensus. This could be split into two PRs to make it easier to test and review.

Make sure that the replay thread doesn't block on the scheduler finishing processing blocks.

Add slot cancellation, where Votor can tell replay which blocks to stop trying to process.

There was an earlier PR (PR #16454) which attempted to solve a similar problem, but that PR included some complexity around being able to pause and resume block processing.

This PR attempts to solve a similar problem in a simpler way by adding slot cancellation. It allows validators to stop replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another block from the same slot has been finalized.

This is an efficiency-focused change to validator software. It's not intended to have a particular effect on transaction throughput or SOL price. For Solana to continue to perform well, it's important not only to continue to increase TPS but also continue to find ways to make sure that validators aren't doing unnecessary work.

For everyday users, it's unlikely there would be noticeable effects from this change. Sending/receiving SOL, using a DEX, using DeFi more broadly, and using any other Solana-powered website/app should all continue to function as normal. It's possible that users could see some benefits from this change in the form of Solana being more performant in the face of heavy compute loads.

#4993. Bitcoin supply in profit falls below 50% – But is BTC’s worst over?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Monday New York trading session open brought a flurry of volatility to Bitcoin [BTC] and the rest of the market. Nvidia’s stock soared 31% after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately.

Combined with the oversold market conditions, the tech and AI-sector stock market bounce helped Bitcoin rally to a local high of $64,603.

Unfortunately for the bulls, the entirety of Monday’s rally has been undone.

At the time of writing, BTC was back below the $61,000 mark. Its rally liquidated $520.89 million in short positions across the crypto market, including $225.58 million for Bitcoin alone.

The BTC spot ETF flows on Monday measured -$60.4 million, extending the bearish market sentiment and highlighting the lack of demand.

The MVRV Z-score measures the difference between market capitalization and realized capitalization. It displayed a reading of 0.24 and has fallen by 0.11 over the past week, reaching among the lowest in four years.

It has remained positive for 1,410 days, reported crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. A drop below zero would mean that the market cap has fallen below realized cap, a sign of deep capitulation.

Another metric that reached some of its lowest levels in four years was the supply in profit. It compares the market price with the last moved price of coins in the circulating supply.

Less than half of the coins are in profit, mirroring the lows from the previous bear market lows of late 2022.

In August, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on Binance peaked at +2.41b. This peak showed heavy market buying as prices climbed toward $80k. Yet, as the price pushed to the local high at $87k, the CVD on Binance declined to -6b.

This was a bearish divergence; rising sell market orders captured take-profit behavior, while late entrants and leverage hunts pushed prices higher.

In November, across all exchanges, the CVD’s decline accelerated alongside price drawdown, and Binance’s CVD figure reached -21b, wrote crypto analyst FundingVest.

If the falling CVD momentum slows down while Bitcoin’s price continues its descent, it could be a constructive sign that will considerably increase the chances of a recovery.

#4991. Bitcoin Reserves Just Found a New Use on Wall Street, but There’s a Catch

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitcoin reserves have found another potential use within the US financial system. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has clarified that regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ethereum and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements. However, the regulator is not prepared to treat those holdings like cash.

The guidance, issued on November 23, could give regulated trading venues greater flexibility in managing their balance sheets. For Bitcoin investors, however, the more interesting question is whether that flexibility will translate into fresh institutional demand.

The answer is not quite as straightforward as it might seem.

The CFTC’s latest advisory addresses three types of regulated businesses: swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations.

These institutions are required to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover at least one year of operating costs. Under the new staff guidance, Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins may contribute toward those requirements, subject to appropriate valuation discounts.

The announcement follows broader efforts to integrate digital assets into regulated financial infrastructure. NewsBTC previously reported on the CFTC’s guidance concerning tokenized collateral at clearinghouses, another area where traditional financial markets are gradually accommodating blockchain-based assets.

This time, the discussion is not about what traders can post as collateral. It is about the assets that the institutions running those markets can rely on to keep their businesses operating.

For a company that already holds Bitcoin, the clarification could make those holdings more useful from a regulatory standpoint. For businesses considering adding cryptocurrency to their balance sheets, it removes some uncertainty surrounding how those assets would be recognized.

But that recognition comes at a discount!

The CFTC advisory references a minimum 20% valuation haircut for Bitcoin and Ethereum, consistent with earlier staff treatment of proprietary cryptocurrency positions held by futures commission merchants.

Qualifying payment stablecoins receive considerably more favorable treatment, with a referenced haircut of 2%.

An exchange holding $10 million in Bitcoin, for example, would be able to count $8 million toward the relevant financial resource requirement if it applied a 20% haircut and no further deductions were necessary.

The remaining $2 million is not a realized loss. It is a regulatory adjustment intended to account for the risk associated with holding a volatile asset.

Crypto assets that are neither readily marketable nor qualifying payment stablecoins would generally face a 100% haircut, effectively excluding them from the calculation.

Perhaps the most revealing part of the advisory is the regulator’s warning about what it calls wrong-way risk.

A DCM should consider potential wrong-way risk

For a cryptocurrency-focused exchange, that risk is particularly relevant. A prolonged Bitcoin sell-off could put pressure on trading revenues while simultaneously reducing the value of the assets the exchange relies on to support its operations.

The problem is not simply that Bitcoin is volatile. It is that its value could deteriorate at precisely the moment a crypto business finds itself under financial pressure.

A 20% valuation discount provides some protection against that scenario, but it is hardly a guarantee.

Despite allowing digital assets to contribute toward broader operating resources, the CFTC has maintained a separate requirement for cash and highly liquid securities.

Bitcoin, Ethereum and even qualifying payment stablecoins cannot be used to satisfy that particular obligation under the advisory.

Swap execution facilities must maintain qualifying liquid resources sufficient to cover at least three months of projected operating expenses or the cost of winding down their operations, whichever is greater.

For designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations, the operating-cost liquidity requirement generally covers at least six months.

The distinction matters because an institution can have substantial assets on its balance sheet without necessarily having the cash available to meet immediate obligations.

It is also worth noting that the guidance does not address whether cryptocurrencies can satisfy the separate financial resources that clearinghouses must maintain to cover clearing-member defaults.

In effect, the CFTC is recognizing Bitcoin as an asset that can contribute to an institution’s financial strength without giving it the same regulatory standing as cash.

That is a more cautious approach than some Bitcoin advocates might have hoped for, but arguably a more sustainable one for integrating cryptocurrency into financial infrastructure.

The bullish interpretation is relatively simple. If regulated financial institutions can derive greater utility from holding Bitcoin, more of them may eventually consider allocating capital to the cryptocurrency.

The expansion of regulated crypto infrastructure has already brought digital assets closer to traditional financial markets. Earlier, NewsBTC reported on Coinbase’s CFTC registration for its USDC-focused derivatives clearinghouse, illustrating how cryptocurrency businesses are increasingly operating within established regulatory frameworks.

The latest advisory gives relevant institutions another reason to evaluate how digital assets fit into their balance sheets.

Still, there is a considerable difference between allowing an institution to hold Bitcoin for regulatory purposes and giving it an economic incentive to buy more.

An exchange that already owns Bitcoin could benefit from the clarification without purchasing a single additional coin. Another might conclude that holding conventional securities remains more efficient, particularly given the valuation discounts and separate liquidity requirements.

Nothing in the advisory requires institutions to acquire Bitcoin, and no purchase commitments were disclosed alongside the announcement.

Investors should therefore resist the temptation to translate this development directly into a bullish price forecast.

The longer-term significance may be greater than the immediate market impact. Every additional recognized use for Bitcoin within regulated financial markets strengthens the case for its utility beyond speculative trading.

However, the November 23 document remains a staff advisory rather than a binding rule adopted by the full Commission. It does not amend existing regulations or create enforceable rights.

The next meaningful development will be evidence that regulated institutions are actually changing their reserve allocations in response.

Until then, Bitcoin has gained another form of regulatory recognition. Whether it gains another source of sustained buying pressure is a different question entirely.

XRP traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a localized sell-off, raising questions about thin liquidity.

XRP reportedly traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a sharp, localized sell-off discussed by crypto commentator Crypto Sensei.

His video examines whether the trades reflected an exchange-specific liquidity problem rather than a broader XRP collapse, alongside falling ledger activity and disputed price forecasts.

According to the account presented in the video, 11 Canadian-dollar markets fell by at least 65%, with bitcoin trading below 18,000 and ether around 560.

The host cites November 20, 2026 as the incident date and reports that Kraken considered the orders correctly processed and would let the trades stand.

The analyst didn’t include trade records or Kraken’s full statement. Those limits matter: the reported 29-cent execution should not be confused with XRP’s prevailing price across exchanges.

Crypto Sensei attributes the dislocation to heavy selling meeting insufficient liquidity. Buyers may have secured steep discounts, while sellers received prices far below those available elsewhere.

“Whoever sold and just got totally wiped out here, I feel for you,” he says. The video does not establish whether individual losses resulted from discretionary sales, automated orders or liquidations.

A separate headline claiming the XRP Ledger had lost 60% of its users also draws scrutiny.

The underlying figure, according to the clarification cited in the YouTube video, was roughly a 63% decline in daily activity, not evidence that a comparable share of holders permanently departed or sold their XRP.

The host challenges Jake Claver’s repeated $100 year-end XRP forecast, arguing that institutional adoption is a longer process than such targets suggest. He also distinguishes Ripple’s business expansion from confirmed institutional use of XRP itself.

Former Ripple executive and Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla offers a longer-term XRP development case in a clip: Evernorth intends to deploy XRP on-chain, pursue yield and support ecosystem features rather than simply hold the asset. The video leaves the execution details and eventual returns unresolved.

For HODLers, these are separate questions: whether an exchange has enough liquidity, whether ledger usage is growing, and whether adoption creates demand for XRP. A dramatic trade print, or an ambitious treasury strategy, does not answer all three.

Onchain Lens reported over $600,000 lost from one user’s Trezor and Exodus wallets on the 23rd of November. The Trezor wallet theft report raised a harder question: how did transfers use the victim’s signing authority without their claimed approval?

The blockchain investigator listed approximately $580,000 in Tether [USDT] losses on TRON and $23,400 in USD Coin [USDC] on Solana. Another $9,500 reportedly disappeared from an Exodus wallet on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max.

Reportedly, the victim generated the recovery phrase on Trezor and kept it on paper and refused to allow anyone physical access to the device.

A 49,999 USDT transfer on the 21st of November used the TRON account’s default owner permission. It was a direct transfer, with no transfer from operation drawing on an existing token allowance.

On Solana [SOL], the examined instruction identified the victim’s wallet as the transfer authority, signer, and fee payer. Notably, no separate delegate appeared.

These transfers used the wallet’s signing authority. However, it is unclear how someone gained that access.

A valid signature authorizes a transaction on the network. So, it cannot establish whether the owner knowingly approved it. The Trezor accounts on both chains shared one recovery phrase, making that backup a possible link between the losses.

In an X reply, Trezor said similar cases usually involved “a compromised wallet backup.”

It’s hard to say what happened here without more details.

The company asked the affected user to contact official support. Its reply offered a possible explanation, without establishing this incident’s cause.

Trezor says its Bluetooth chip cannot access private keys. On the other hand, Exodus says its Trezor integration also leaves those keys inside the hardware. Whether the user enabled that integration remains unclear.

Apple’s 9th of November update patched Bluetooth issues, but Onchain Lens found no evidence linking those vulnerabilities to these transfers.

Earlier incidents show why identifying the route matters.

As AMBCrypto reported, Trezor confirmed implants in three CryptoBilis-sold Safe 5 devices on the 12th of November. Those implants captured recovery words from device screens.

Separately, Confiant’s MoldyRoost research documented another route; malicious ads delivering exploits to vulnerable iPhones. Furthermore, Chainalysis counted roughly 158,000 personal-wallet compromise incidents affecting 80,000 victims in 2025.

For this user, the unanswered question is specific: how did someone obtain signing access across the affected wallets?

#4987. Binance Hack: US Moves to Recover $1.1 Billion, but Who Gets the Money?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Nearly four weeks after the Binance hack, US authorities have filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October theft. The money is already subject to restrictions, but the latest court filings reveal a complication: freezing stolen cryptocurrency is considerably easier than returning it.

The complaint, filed on November 23, in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, targets USDC associated with 36 cryptocurrency addresses across 18 blockchains.

Federal investigators attribute the October 29 attack to North Korean hacking groups, including the Lazarus Group. The complaint puts the value of the original theft at approximately $6 billion.

For Binance, the latest legal action represents another opportunity to recover a portion of its losses. For the wider cryptocurrency industry, however, the case raises questions about the authority stablecoin issuers exercise over digital assets and what happens when governments become involved.

The assets targeted by US authorities are not an entirely new discovery.

Earlier this month, NewsBTC reported that Circle had frozen approximately $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Binance hack, following cooperation with law enforcement.

What has changed is the government’s attempt to establish a legal basis for taking possession of those assets.

According to the court documents, US authorities obtained a temporary restraining order on November 12. Prosecutors subsequently requested that the restrictions remain in place throughout the civil forfeiture proceedings.

Both Binance and Circle consented to the initial restraining order and the requested extension, according to the government’s November 23 application.

The agreement between the companies and federal authorities reduces one immediate obstacle to preserving the funds. It does not, however, resolve the question of their ultimate ownership or distribution.

Civil forfeiture proceedings are directed against property believed to be connected to criminal activity. Interested parties can assert legitimate claims to that property through the legal process.

In this case, prosecutors are seeking forfeiture of the assets to the United States. That is not the same thing as a court ordering their immediate return to Binance.

Perhaps the most interesting disclosure in the complaint concerns Circle itself.

The stablecoin issuer can restrict transfers involving USDC held at particular blockchain addresses. However, that authority does not necessarily give Circle direct control over the wallets holding those tokens.

does not have the technical ability to transfer the Defendant Property from the blocklisted Subject Addresses to the United States

Instead, Circle has agreed to issue an equivalent amount of replacement USDC and transfer those tokens to US authorities upon receiving a forfeiture order from the court.

The proposed arrangement exposes an unusual feature of centralized stablecoins. An issuer can prevent tokens from circulating without possessing the private keys needed to move them.

It also raises an accounting question that deserves attention. If replacement tokens are issued, what ultimately happens to the original frozen USDC, and how will Circle ensure that the treatment of those balances is reflected accurately in its outstanding supply and reserve reporting?

The issuance of replacement tokens would not, by itself, prove that USDC had become undercollateralized. Nevertheless, transparency around the implementation would be important for a stablecoin whose credibility depends on confidence in its backing.

The immediate concern is not whether Circle can create new tokens. It is whether the entire recovery process can be independently accounted for.

The temptation to describe the Justice Department’s announcement as a billion-dollar recovery is understandable. It is also premature.

There are three separate stages involved: restricting access to the stolen assets, obtaining legal authority over them and determining how they will ultimately be distributed.

The November 23 filings advance the second stage. They do not establish that the third has been completed.

There is also a cross-border complication.

On November 18, Reuters reported that an Abu Dhabi court had directed several cryptocurrency companies, including Circle, to preserve digital assets associated with the Binance theft.

The involvement of authorities in both the United States and the United Arab Emirates illustrates how a single cryptocurrency theft can generate legal proceedings across multiple jurisdictions.

Blockchain transactions may cross national borders without much difficulty. Establishing ownership rights over the assets involved is a considerably less straightforward exercise.

That does not mean the US and UAE proceedings are necessarily in conflict. But the ultimate disposition of the funds will require more than an announcement from either government.

For investors assessing Binance’s financial position, the distinction between frozen assets and recovered capital is particularly important. Restricted cryptocurrency should not automatically be treated as money already returned to the exchange.

For years, the ability of stablecoin issuers to freeze tokens has been criticized by advocates of decentralized finance.

The Binance case demonstrates the other side of that argument.

Without Circle’s ability to restrict transactions, preserving such a large amount of cryptocurrency for potential recovery would have been more difficult.

In this particular case, centralized control has provided a mechanism that may help prevent suspected criminals from benefiting from stolen assets.

The uncomfortable question is whether the cryptocurrency industry can benefit from that authority while also demanding meaningful safeguards against its misuse.

The answer depends partly on transparency. Token holders should be able to understand why assets were frozen, under what legal authority restrictions remain in place and how disputes over ownership are resolved.

The same standard should apply to the exchange, the stablecoin issuer and the government.

The next significant development in the Binance case will be the court’s treatment of the forfeiture claim and any competing claims to the assets. Circle’s proposed issuance of replacement USDC will also deserve scrutiny if it proceeds.

Until then, the $1.1 billion should be understood as assets subject to an ongoing recovery effort, not a completed repayment.

For a cryptocurrency industry that frequently celebrates the speed of moving money, the Binance hack is a reminder that getting it back can be an entirely different business.
